chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Sari ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
He said: When God wishes good for a servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when God wishes evil for a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets them on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection / Judgment Day

ai.seo_question: Why does God punish believers in this world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the concept of 'tad'een' (delaying punishment) as a sign of divine mercy, where believers' sins are expiated through worldly trials to preserve their full reward in the Hereafter. Conversely, the accumulation of sins for the Day of Judgment indicates a different divine decree, often interpreted by Shia scholars as a test of endurance or a means to increase reward for those who remain steadfast despite their faults.
